hints.title: 1 · Measure the whole response
hints.body: Capture sql.active_record around the request, including serialization. Count queries as the page size grows. Determine separately whether tenant filtering and pagination happen before records are loaded.

hints.title: 2 · Load relationships deliberately
hints.body: For a fictional Article list: Article.where(team_id: identity).order(id: :desc).limit(limit + 1).preload(:writer). Query related counts in one GROUP BY keyed by page IDs. This avoids both per-row lookups and loading every child record.

hints.title: 3 · Use one extra row for the next cursor
hints.body: Fetch limit + 1 to detect another page; return only limit and use its final ID as the next cursor if more exist. A valid cursor means id < cursor, not offset. Check exactly-full pages, empty pages, malformed inputs, and multiple authors.

criteria.title: Pagination and response correctness
criteria.target: Descending cursor pages preserve every item exactly once on a stable dataset; fields and counts remain exact.
criteria.probe: Why is next_cursor nil on an exactly full final page?
criteria.practice: Implement keyset pagination with a limit-plus-one query.

criteria.title: Identity and input boundaries
criteria.target: Tenant identity comes only from the supplied gateway header and malformed pagination is rejected.
criteria.probe: Could an arbitrary valid cursor expose another tenant?
criteria.practice: Test cross-tenant data mixed among page boundaries.

criteria.title: Bounded data access
criteria.target: At most four data SELECTs; SQL bounds posts; comments are aggregated without individual instantiation.
criteria.probe: How can a constant query count still have unbounded memory cost?
criteria.practice: Compare query count, rows scanned, and records instantiated.

criteria.title: Performance investigation
criteria.target: Claims cite measured queries and explain indexes/query plans without replacing evidence with a timing guess.
criteria.probe: Which indexes would support the tenant cursor and comment count queries?
criteria.practice: Explain an EXPLAIN plan and distinguish local test evidence from production latency.

follow_up: Recommend and measure indexes on (organization_id, id) and comments.post_id. Discuss cursor consistency under inserts/deletes, query plans at millions of rows, and when denormalized counters are worth their write complexity.
